geothermal-plant-heat-pump.alt: Two panels. Left: a geothermal power plant. Steam and hot water rise from hot rock up a production well to spin a turbine connected to a generator that sends out electricity; cooled water returns down an injection well. The hot rock is heated by Earth's interior through radioactive decay and heat left from Earth's formation. Right: a house with a heat pump connected to a U-shaped pipe loop buried a few meters down, where the ground stays about the same temperature all year; in winter heat moves from the ground to the house, in summer from the house to the ground.
